transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-02 16:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maxine Lowe (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Hannah Ortiz (Velorum CTO), Markus Feld (Velorum Lead ML), Priya Iyer (Velorum DevOps), Sam (Velorum Product)

Summary (auto): quick hosted API walkthrough focused on streaming chat, setting params for latency/cost, and safe retry patterns. Security constraints (PHI, VPC, KMS) came up early; we agreed to a sandbox POC.

[00:00] Maxine: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick intro, im maxine, im the AE. ethan will do the deep demo. can i get a 30 second round from velorum?
[00:12] Hannah: sure. hannah here, cto. we're building a patient intake triage bot, biggest concerns around latency and PHI, also cost at scale.
[00:22] Markus: Markus, lead ML, we run inference on-prem for redacted records today, but open to cloud if we can meet isolation controls.
[00:33] Priya: priya, devops, will need details on networking/VPC, egress, and key management.
[00:42] Maxine: perfect, thanks. ethan, over to you.
[00:45] Ethan: cool. i'll share my screen, i'm going to do a stream-first walkthrough of a simple chat flow, show the streaming socket behavior, typical params to tune, and then the retry/backoff playbook. starting with a short example prompt — patient says symptoms, we do follow-up Qs.
[01:05] Ethan: (typing) so the hosted endpoint we call is /v1/chat.stream — stream returns deltas, you can render progressively. important: tokens are billed for final tokens generated, partial chunks still show but you only pay final usage (some small nuance if you abort early).
[01:22] Markus: small interruption — you said billing only for final tokens, but we saw some providers charge for all streamed bytes. is that definite?
[01:30] Ethan: yes, with redwood hosted it's per-response tokens; if you cancel mid-response you'll be billed for what's generated up to cancel. there are nuances for embeddings and other endpoints but for chat it's per-token.
[01:40] Hannah: ok good. next, what's the best way to keep latency under 600ms for short followups?
[01:48] Ethan: great question. two levers: model selection and batch size / concurrency. choose a low-latency model variant (we recommend the <redwood-low-latency-1> family for short contexts), and use small max_new_tokens + prefix caching. prefix/K-V cache is huge — if your flows have repeated system prompts or similar histories we keep KV cache hot and skip re-computation.
[02:10] Ethan: also set streaming chunk_size to 64 or 128 to reduce RTTs for your frontend. and reduce temperature if you want determinism.
[02:22] Priya: prefix cache — does that work across dedicated and hosted? and any PII concerns?
[02:30] Ethan: it works in hosted and Dedicated, and in Private we let you manage cache retention. prefix cache stores KV vectors in RAM on the serving node; we encrypt in transit and at rest for hosted. for PHI we recommend Private or Dedicated with customer-managed KMS.
[02:47] Hannah: so sounds like private is preferred; but we wanted to try hosted sandbox first to validate latency. is there an option to pin model and then move to private?
[02:55] Ethan: absolutely — same API surface, you can pin model versions and then flip the deployment target.
[03:03] Maxine: quick clarification on retries — what should we do in the client when a stream fails mid-response?
[03:09] Ethan: best practice: make your client idempotent at the request level. attach a client_request_id, and on server errors attempt a retry with exponential backoff. for streamed responses, we provide resume tokens for certain cases — but common pattern is check if response partial is useful; if not, retry from start with same idempotency key. keep retries limited (start with 250ms, 2x backoff, max 8s, and cap retries at 3).
[03:36] Markus: resume tokens? i thought streaming was stateless per call.
[03:40] Ethan: correct, most calls are stateless; resume tokens are for long-running generation checkpoints in dedicated/private—less common. for hosted we lean on short retries and auto-fallback to smaller model variant if capacity issues.
[03:54] Priya: how do auto-fallbacks work? if the low-latency model is busy, will you silently route to a cheaper one?
[04:00] Ethan: we route by policy. you can set route preference: prefer-low-latency then fallback-to-cost-optimized. we surface headers so you can detect when fallback occurred, and console shows per-request trace. we do not silently change model without traceability.
[04:15] Sam: is there a way to test failover during our integration tests?
[04:18] Ethan: yes, we expose a chaos flag in sandbox to simulate slow nodes and capacity errors so you can validate client retry behavior.
[04:28] Hannah: security stuff — SOC2 and SAML SSO?
[04:31] Maxine: we have SOC 2 Type II, SAML/SSO, RBAC, and audit logs. we'll send the security brief after the call: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2.pdf and an SSO setup doc.
[04:44] Hannah: and KMS integration? we must maintain control of keys for PHI.
[04:48] Ethan: hosted can integrate with customer KMS for Dedicated/private; for hosted we use our managed key but we offer bring-your-own-key on Dedicated. for full on-prem you can run the Private package.
[04:59] Markus: network egress — what ports and peering requirements?
[05:03] Ethan: typical egress is outbound HTTPS to our ingestion endpoints. for Private/Dedicated we support VPC peering and private connectivity; priya we can provide a network runbook after this call.
[05:15] Priya: please do. also curious about tokenization and truncation. if a user submits a 4k prompt exceed model context, what's recommended?
[05:22] Ethan: we recommend pre-tokenization on client side, and run a truncation policy: preserve recent messages, compress system prompt via embedding + retrieval for long histories. Optimize has tooling to suggest where to trim and when to cache.
[05:35] Maxine: small demo — ethan, can you show a live stream and then force a retry so they see client experience?
[05:40] Ethan: yep. starting a sample request now. (typing) streaming chunks coming in... [05:50] chunk: "Follow-up: Have you experienced fever?" ... now i'm artificially blocking the stream to simulate a timeout — you should see the client try backoff.
[06:05] Sam: i see partial text and then it retries, UI shows spinner, then full response returns. good.
[06:12] Ethan: note the client_request_id header; in the logs you'll see trace id and whether fallback happened.
[06:20] Hannah: how do we measure per-route latency in console?
[06:23] Ethan: console exposes per-model and per-route percentiles, token-level billing, and a flamegraph of time spent in model decode vs queuing. we'll show that in optimize later.
[06:33] Markus: cost question — how much savings can prefix caching and batching do?
[06:37] Ethan: depends on pattern. for repeated system prompts and short follow-ups, caching can cut prompt compute by 30-70%. batching helps throughput but increases tail latency; for user-facing short chat keep batch size small and rely on caching. Optimize will give model-specific quantization and batch suggestions.
[06:56] Priya: any caveats with quantized models and hallucination rates?
[07:00] Ethan: yes, quantization can slightly increase hallucination in some model families; Optimize runs evals on your prompt set to recommend quantization profiles that balance cost vs quality.
[07:12] Hannah: blockers for us: 1) want to validate 500-800ms p95 in our EU region, 2) must confirm KMS + VPC options, 3) need to quantify cost per monthly MAU.
[07:24] Maxine: actionable — we'll send a latency/cost spreadsheet and a sandbox curl snippet. we'll also set up a POC scoping call next week with infra & security.
[07:32] Ethan: i'll include the sandbox chaos flag example and the streaming snippet. quick note on idempotency: use the "x-client-request-id" header, store partials locally and reconcile on retry.
[07:44] Markus: about long-term ops — if we move to Dedicated later, will we need to rework client code?
[07:49] Ethan: no, same API. you may change endpoint host but request params and semantics remain identical. we keep SDK compatibility.
[07:58] Priya: can we get sample logs to see what a partial failure looks like?
[08:01] Ethan: yes i'll attach a sample trace log.
[08:05] Maxine: okay — final five minute recap.
[08:08] Hannah: liked the chaos flag idea. want to run smoke tests in hosted sandbox first, then scoped POC in Dedicated if pass.
[08:16] Maxine: next steps recap: ethan share sandbox curl + code (due tues), maxine share pricing/checklist (due tues), hannah send prompts (due wed), priya confirm networking (due thurs). we've got a POC scoping call penciled for 2025-05-09.
[08:30] Sam: quick Q — any competitors we should benchmark against?
[08:33] Maxine: customers often look at OpenAI and Anthropic for quality and AWS SageMaker if they want full infra control; we'll share a comparison doc.
[08:40] Hannah: thanks, that's helpful.
[08:42] Maxine: thanks everyone. we'll follow up via email with the deck and links: https://redwood.ai/decks/velorum-hosted-demo and the security brief.
[08:51] Markus: bye all.

Notes:
- Shared artifacts: deck link (above), security brief link, sandbox curl snippet (to be sent).
- Transcription imperfections: speaker overlaps and some tech names mistranscribed (e.g., K-V cache, quantiz).

End of transcript.
